_provenance: Every chart in the examples below is constructed synthetic data for demonstrating a switch.

examples: Baseline body positions for a Munich subject born 1991-11-04 at 13:00 local (Placidus, tropical): astrolog -qj 2448565.000000 -zl 11:34E 48:08N -c 0 -v0
Sidereal baseline for a Sydney-born subject (whole-sign houses): astrolog -qj 2459580.500000 -zl 151:12E 33:52S -c 14 -s -v0
Quick-birth fallback for a New York subject at 7:45 am on 4 July 1976 with DST flagged: astrolog -qb 7 4 1976 7:45am 1 5W 73:56W 40:43N -c 0 -v0
gotchas: The quick-birth time anchor carries a standalone DST flag and integer-hour offset; if the subject's zone lookup never populated a base offset or DST rule, the invocation silently drifts by an hour rather than failing loudly.
Coordinate formatting rounds to whole arcminutes, so two subjects within ~1 km of each other produce identical argv — don't rely on the command string as a precise locator.

Biwheel and multi-chart layers reorder the base parameters (location must precede the time anchor); copy-pasting a single-subject invocation into a multi-wheel context without reshuffling causes astrolog to ignore either the location or the second anchor.

Body-restriction switches are position-sensitive relative to the mode switch: appending extra on/off toggles after -v0 can flip the output mode or silently re-enable bodies the caller meant to suppress.
heuristics: Prefer the Julian-day form (-qj <jd>) over the quick-birth form (-qb ...) for any single-subject calculation so the invocation is DST-independent.
When using -qj, always follow it with -zl <lon> <lat> so angle-dependent outputs have a reference location.
Emit coordinates as degrees:arcminutes with a cardinal suffix (E/W for longitude, N/S for latitude); never pass decimal degrees.
Always emit the house-system switch -c <code> explicitly, even when the subject uses the built-in default, so the invocation is self-describing.
Tropical zodiac is the implicit default and emits no switch; sidereal requires the -s switch.
For a baseline body-position listing, close the invocation with -v0 (positions plus relative velocity), not bare -v.
Layer body-restriction toggles (per-object on/off switches) before the final output-mode switch so mode selection is the last thing astrolog sees.

hidden_constants.justification: Baseline body listing is emitted with the velocity-aware body-positions mode rather than the plain bodies switch.
hidden_constants.name: default_output_mode_switch

hidden_constants.justification: Placidus maps to house-code 0 and is the default when the subject does not override it.
hidden_constants.name: default_house_code

hidden_constants.justification: Julian-day argument is formatted with six decimal places, giving sub-second resolution.
hidden_constants.name: julian_day_decimal_precision

hidden_constants.justification: Longitude and latitude are truncated-then-rounded to whole arcminutes (~1.8 km at the equator) before formatting.
hidden_constants.name: coordinate_rounding_unit_arcminutes

hidden_constants.justification: When longitude or latitude is within 1e-4 of zero, the cardinal letter defaults to E or N respectively.
hidden_constants.name: greenwich_equator_default_direction

hidden_constants.justification: Internally-stored base offset uses the opposite sign of the standard convention; any conversion to the readable E/W form must negate.
hidden_constants.name: timezone_offset_sign_inversion

astrolog-positions-baseline-invocation.intent: Assemble the astrolog command-line that produces the default body-position listing for one subject at a given moment and place.
post_conditions: Stdout contains a tabular body listing whose rows cover each object left enabled by the body-restriction switches.
Every body row carries an ecliptic longitude expressed as sign plus degrees plus arcminutes and a signed relative velocity.
Exit status is zero on success; any non-zero status with empty stdout signals a malformed invocation (missing location, bad JD, unknown house code, etc.).
The argv must include exactly one time anchor (either a Julian-day anchor or a quick-birth anchor, never both) and exactly one output-mode switch.
When coordinates are present, they match the degrees:arcminutes plus cardinal-letter shape; decimal degrees must not leak through.

examples: Compute the first-call transits chart at the acquired place for the current moment (UT JD derived from wall clock in Go; PlaceInfo lat/lon already resolved by a one-time -zN at atlas-modal Enter): astrolog -qj 2461150.19 -zl 8.7333 52.85
Compute the natal chart for a stored last-used birth moment and location (Unit #1 natal-SET branch; PlaceInfo from the chart record, not re-resolved): astrolog -qj 2446232.0208 -zl 11.567 48.133
gotchas: The first-call chart path never feeds a city string at render time — acquisition already produced PlaceInfo (lat, lon, tz, IANA) via one-time -zN; subsequent chart computes feed those coordinates through -zl. Re-invoking -zN on every render would re-hit the atlas and silently drop offline capability.

The aspect panel's A/S suffix is computed by a finite-difference probe (orb tighter at t+ε = applying), NOT from astrolog's orb sign — that sign is geometric (side-of-exact), not direction. Do not 'flip' astrolog's raw output; it never encoded applying/separating in the first place (verified vs astrolog 7.80; see docs D13).

Column count in the aspect panel is a function of the terminal width and the 15-char cell size; making the pane narrower silently truncates low-strength aspects off the right edge rather than scrolling — the data is not lost, just invisible.
heuristics: Sextile opens into exactly one of three stable states, driven by store contents — not by argv, not by ambient environment. natal-SET (store has a last-used Chart): render that Chart's natal positions with current-moment transits overlaid, composed at ui via tea.Batch fan-in-once (MINDSET §16). natal-UNSET with store.Location populated: render a here-now chart at the stored place. natal-UNSET with no stored location: open the centered atlas-pick modal over an empty shell.

Location acquisition (cold-start cascade, natal-UNSET) is a one-time astrolog -v -n -zN <city> at atlas-modal Enter. Its output is parsed into PlaceInfo (lat, lon, tz, IANA name) and persisted to store.Location. All subsequent chart computes for the session feed those coordinates through -qj {jd_ut} -zl {lon} {lat} — no further -zN calls.

Atlas-modal preseed is a narrow current-Linux-host convenience: if time.Local.String()'s IANA last segment is plausible as a city name, preseed the modal's fzf filter with it; otherwise open a bare modal. No tz→atlas-city alias table is baked; the preseed is a string hint only and the user completes the pick.

Body rendering uses a fixed order: the ten luminaries/planets, then Chiron, then the lunar nodes (north then south), then Lilith; the four angles (Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, Imum Coeli) are always pinned as a separate block at the bottom of the table.

Aspects are sorted by strength (power) descending before laying out column-major (top-to-bottom, then left-to-right) into fixed 15-character cells; the applying/separating flag comes from a finite-difference orb probe at t+ε, not from astrolog's geometric orb sign.

hidden_constants.justification: Trace shows exactly 14 regular body rows (Sun through Lilith) before the angle block, matching the canonical luminaries+planets+Chiron+nodes+Lilith set.
hidden_constants.name: default_body_set_count

hidden_constants.justification: Four angles are always rendered in fixed order regardless of chart: Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, Imum Coeli.
hidden_constants.name: angle_row_count

hidden_constants.justification: Aspect text is formatted to fit a 15-character cell so a 120-column pane yields seven columns per row, confirmed by the seven-per-row layout in the observed aspects panel.
hidden_constants.name: aspect_cell_width_chars

hidden_constants.justification: Single-space gutter between aspect cells, visible in the trace as single-space separation between 15-char aspect tokens.
hidden_constants.name: aspect_cell_gutter_chars

hidden_constants.justification: Trace shows the U+211E prescription-like glyph appended directly after the minute mark for retrograde bodies (e.g. Lilith in Scorpio in the first frame).
hidden_constants.name: retrograde_glyph

first-call-state-presentation.intent: Produce the data that populates the first stable state Sextile renders after cold start. Three branches keyed off store (natal + location), never off environment or machine-tz fallbacks: natal-SET renders the stored Chart's natal positions with current-moment transits overlaid; natal-UNSET with stored location renders a here-now chart at that place; natal-UNSET with no stored location opens the atlas-pick modal. All chart computes for the session use coordinates resolved by a one-time astrolog -zN at modal Enter; no re-resolution per render.
post_conditions: Output must contain every body in the default set plus all four angles — exactly 18 position rows in total for a non-harmonic first frame.
Every parsed body row yields a degree in [0,30) and a minute in [0,60); a violation indicates a malformed position line.
Every aspect entry must reference two bodies that also appear in the position list (no dangling symbols).
The aspects list, after the producer's sort, must be monotonically non-increasing in strength.

The rendered header's place string equals the name field of the PlaceInfo resolved at acquisition (from the one-time astrolog -zN output for the picked city); no synthetic fallback string is substituted, and the place string never changes mid-session without a subsequent acquisition.

intent-rules-keystroke-to-ir.argv_template: (no astrolog invocation — this capability produces an intent token that downstream packages translate into an astrolog command line; a typical downstream rendering looks like: astrolog -qb {yyyy} {mm} {dd} {hh.hhhh} {zone} {lat} {lon} -n0 -Yn0 {extra_switches})
examples: User taps the day-forward letter while on the chart panel with no modal open, yielding the time-nudge intent, which the recipe renders as: astrolog -qb 1990 5 14 12.5 0 52.37 4.89 -n0 -Yn0
User taps the transit-search letter while focused on a body row, which eventually issues: astrolog -qb 1990 5 14 12.5 0 52.37 4.89 -dm -n0 -Yn0

User presses the space bar on a second chart row while one wheel is already pinned, causing selection count to rise to 2 and a multi-wheel bake like: astrolog -qb 1990 5 14 12.5 0 52.37 4.89 -r2 1995 8 3 9.0 0 52.37 4.89 -n0 -Yn0
gotchas: The first-match-wins traversal is stable: if two rows share the same key and context but differ only in guard, swapping their order silently changes which one wins when both pass.
View-only rows are invisible outside their declared view even when the key is unambiguous globally — a user on a different panel sees nothing happen and gets no feedback.
The shifted variant of a chord lives as a separate row; if the shift modifier is ever normalised away upstream, the shifted intent becomes unreachable without any error.
Modal-active suppresses almost every binding via the universal predicate; forgetting to clear that flag after a modal dismissal strands the user with a seemingly dead keyboard.
Time nudges are hard-coded durations, not calendar-aware: a year step is 8760 hours, which drifts on leap years and surprises anyone expecting civil-calendar arithmetic.
The pinned-wheel guard blocks the toggle silently once the cap is hit — there is no rejected-intent event, just no intent at all.
heuristics: Evaluate rows in declared order and accept the first whose key, modifier, context, view-focus, and guard chain all hold — later duplicates are dead weight.
Treat a null/absent guard as unconditionally satisfied; never fabricate one.
Rows flagged view-only apply only when the currently focused view name equals the row's context tag; global rows without that flag apply everywhere.
Build the interaction snapshot fresh at every keystroke from registry, modal, and view state; never cache it across ticks.
When the modal-active flag is set, suppress nearly every intent except the modal's own escape/submit keys (the universal NoModal predicate gates the majority of bindings).
Generate the ten time-nudge rows programmatically from a signed-duration table — lowercase letter = forward, uppercase = backward, magnitudes year/month/day/hour/minute.
Keep the upper bound on pinned wheels at the hidden numeric constant below; exceeding it silently drops the toggle-pin intent via guard failure.
Expose a separate lookup that enumerates every binding valid in a given view — consumers use it to render help overlays without re-running dispatch.

hidden_constants.justification: The multi-wheel cap baked into the selection guard, matching astrolog's -r2..-r6 range.

hidden_constants.justification: One Julian year approximated as 24*365 hours, used as the coarsest forward/backward time step.

hidden_constants.justification: 30-day month approximation used for month-scale time navigation.

hidden_constants.justification: Day-scale time step.

intent-rules-keystroke-to-ir.intent: Translate a raw keystroke plus current interaction snapshot into a named intent token by scanning an ordered table of binding rows whose guard predicates pass.
post_conditions: Exactly one intent token is produced per keystroke, or none — never two.
The emitted intent's declared effect tags are a subset of the fixed effect-tag vocabulary above.
When a modal is flagged active, no intent with side-effects outside the modal surface is emitted.
The pinned-wheel count never exceeds the hidden max_pinned_wheels constant after a toggle-pin intent resolves.
Time-nudge intents parse back to a signed duration whose absolute value is one of the five nudge constants.
Help/enumeration queries by view never include rows whose context tag contradicts the queried view.
Undo/redo intents fire only when the corresponding history stack is non-empty at dispatch time.
The transit-search intent fires only when the bodies panel is focused and a specific celestial body is highlighted.
